Income growth rates

Use income growth data sample_growth_tb to plot density curves and mean excess functions for annual growth rates and growth rates over each period starting in 2014. After applying common income and age conditions, density estimation and mean excess calculations use different additional restrictions.

1 Density estimation

library(tidyverse)
library(pins)

# Specify relative paths for the board, figure output directory, and plotting theme.
board <- board_folder("../income_board_replicate")
graph_dir <- "graph"
dir.create(graph_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
source("theme_ipsum_like.R")
theme_set(theme_ipsum())

Data loading and sample selection

Load sample_growth_tb and select observations meeting the following conditions for each period.

  • Beginning-of-period income pre_income of at least \(4 \times 10^6\) yen (4 million yen)
  • Beginning-of-period age \(25 \leq \mathrm{age} \leq 60\)

Calculate age as the beginning year extracted from period label year minus the birth year in the first four characters of birth_date. Do not add industry-based exclusions.

library(scattermore)

sample_growth_tb <- board |> pin_read("sample_growth_tb") |> 
  mutate(age = as.numeric(str_c(20, str_sub(year,6,7))) - as.numeric(str_sub(birth_date, 1, 4))) |> 
  filter(pre_income >= 4*10^6, 
         age >= 25, age <= 60)

year_labels <- c(
  "g_20_19" = "2019–20",
  "g_19_18" = "2018–19",
  "g_18_17" = "2017–18",
  "g_17_16" = "2016–17",
  "g_16_15" = "2015–16",
  "g_15_14" = "2014–15",
  "g_16_14" = "2014–16",
  "g_17_14" = "2014–17",
  "g_18_14" = "2014–18",
  "g_19_14" = "2014–19",
  "g_20_14" = "2014–20"
)

Annual growth distributions by period

  • Compare six annual growth rates from 2014–15 through 2019–20
  • For density plots only, additionally require nonzero growth with an absolute value below 3.5
  • Output two figures, with density on a linear and a logarithmic vertical scale

Use a linear horizontal scale for growth rates in both figures. For the linear-density figure, display growth from −1 to 1; for the log-density figure, display growth from −2 to 2 and density from \(10^{-3}\) to \(10^{1.5}\).

growth_df_plot <- sample_growth_tb |>  
  filter(year %in% c("g_20_19", "g_19_18", "g_18_17", "g_17_16", "g_16_15", "g_15_14"), 
         abs(growth) < 3.5, growth != 0) |>  
ggplot() + 
  geom_density(aes(growth, color = year)) + 
  scale_color_viridis_d(
    option = "C",
    labels = year_labels
  ) 

growth_df_plot + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1.0,1.0)) + 
  labs(
      x = "Growth Rate",
      y = "Density (normal scale)", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "growth_df_main_var_diff_year.png", path = graph_dir)
growth_df_plot + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2.0,2.0), ylim = c(10^{-3.0}, 10^{1.5})) + 
  labs(
      x = "Growth Rate",
      y = "Density (log scale)", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "growth_df_main_var_diff_year_log.png", path = graph_dir)

Growth distributions for periods starting in 2014

  • Compare six periods starting in 2014, from 2014–15 through 2014–20
  • As in the annual growth density plots, use observations with nonzero growth and an absolute value below 3.5
  • Output two figures, with density on a linear and a logarithmic vertical scale

Use the same scales and display ranges as in the annual growth figures.

growth_long_plot <- sample_growth_tb |>  
  filter(str_sub(year, 6, 7) == "14",
         abs(growth) < 3.5, growth != 0) |> 
ggplot() + 
  geom_density(aes(growth, color = year)) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(
    option = "C",
    labels = year_labels
  ) 

growth_long_plot + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1.0, 1.0)) + 
  labs(
      x = "Growth Rate",
      y = "Density (normal scale)", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "long_term_growth_df_main_var.png", path = graph_dir)
growth_long_plot + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2.0,2.0), ylim = c(10^{-3.0}, 10^{1.5})) + 
  labs(
      x = "Growth Rate",
      y = "Density (log scale)", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "long_term_growth_df_main_var_log.png", path = graph_dir)

2 Mean Excess Function

Plot mean excess functions separately for annual growth rates and growth rates over periods starting in 2014. Use data satisfying the common income and age conditions, without applying the zero-growth and absolute-value restrictions used only for the density plots.

Sort growth in descending order, \(g_{(1)}\geq\cdots\geq g_{(n)}\), and calculate the following expression.

\[\widehat m_j=\frac{1}{j-1}\sum_{i=1}^{j-1}g_{(i)}-g_{(j)}, \qquad j\geq2.\]

Plot the growth threshold on the horizontal axis and m_excess on the vertical axis, using colors to distinguish periods. Display horizontal ranges of 0.1–3 for annual growth and 0.1–4 for growth over periods starting in 2014, with a vertical range of 0–1 in both figures. Include growth rates outside the displayed range in the calculations.

mean_excess_plot_f <- \(x){
  x |>
    arrange(desc(growth)) |> 
    group_by(year) |> 
    mutate(m_excess = lag(cummean(growth)) - growth) |> 
  ggplot(aes(growth, m_excess, color = year)) +
    geom_scattermore(pointsize = 1.2) + 
    scale_color_viridis_d(
      option = "C",
      labels = year_labels
    ) 
}

sample_growth_tb |> 
  filter(year %in% c("g_20_19", "g_19_18", "g_18_17", "g_17_16", "g_16_15", "g_15_14")) |>  
  mean_excess_plot_f() + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1, 3.0), ylim = c(0, 1.0)) + 
  labs(
      x = "Threshold u",
      y = "Mean Excess", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "mean_excess_main_var_diff_year.png", path = graph_dir)

sample_growth_tb |>  
  filter(str_sub(year, 6, 7) == "14") |> 
  mean_excess_plot_f() + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1, 4.0), ylim = c(0, 1.0)) + 
  labs(
      x = "Threshold u",
      y = "Mean Excess", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "mean_excess_main_var_long_growth.png", path = graph_dir)

Use income growth data `sample_growth_tb` to plot density curves and mean excess functions for annual growth rates and growth rates over each period starting in 2014.
After applying common income and age conditions, density estimation and mean excess calculations use different additional restrictions.

## 1 Density estimation

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(pins)

# Specify relative paths for the board, figure output directory, and plotting theme.
board <- board_folder("../income_board_replicate")
graph_dir <- "graph"
dir.create(graph_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
source("theme_ipsum_like.R")
theme_set(theme_ipsum())
```

**Data loading and sample selection**

Load `sample_growth_tb` and select observations meeting the following conditions for each period.

* Beginning-of-period income `pre_income` of at least $4 \times 10^6$ yen (4 million yen)
* Beginning-of-period age $25 \leq \mathrm{age} \leq 60$

Calculate age as the beginning year extracted from period label `year` minus the birth year in the first four characters of `birth_date`.
Do not add industry-based exclusions.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

library(scattermore)

sample_growth_tb <- board |> pin_read("sample_growth_tb") |> 
  mutate(age = as.numeric(str_c(20, str_sub(year,6,7))) - as.numeric(str_sub(birth_date, 1, 4))) |> 
  filter(pre_income >= 4*10^6, 
         age >= 25, age <= 60)

year_labels <- c(
  "g_20_19" = "2019–20",
  "g_19_18" = "2018–19",
  "g_18_17" = "2017–18",
  "g_17_16" = "2016–17",
  "g_16_15" = "2015–16",
  "g_15_14" = "2014–15",
  "g_16_14" = "2014–16",
  "g_17_14" = "2014–17",
  "g_18_14" = "2014–18",
  "g_19_14" = "2014–19",
  "g_20_14" = "2014–20"
)

```

**Annual growth distributions by period**

* Compare six annual growth rates from 2014–15 through 2019–20
* For density plots only, additionally require nonzero growth with an absolute value below 3.5
* Output two figures, with density on a linear and a logarithmic vertical scale

Use a linear horizontal scale for growth rates in both figures.
For the linear-density figure, display growth from −1 to 1; for the log-density figure, display growth from −2 to 2 and density from $10^{-3}$ to $10^{1.5}$.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

growth_df_plot <- sample_growth_tb |>  
  filter(year %in% c("g_20_19", "g_19_18", "g_18_17", "g_17_16", "g_16_15", "g_15_14"), 
         abs(growth) < 3.5, growth != 0) |>  
ggplot() + 
  geom_density(aes(growth, color = year)) + 
  scale_color_viridis_d(
    option = "C",
    labels = year_labels
  ) 

growth_df_plot + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1.0,1.0)) + 
  labs(
      x = "Growth Rate",
      y = "Density (normal scale)", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "growth_df_main_var_diff_year.png", path = graph_dir)
growth_df_plot + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2.0,2.0), ylim = c(10^{-3.0}, 10^{1.5})) + 
  labs(
      x = "Growth Rate",
      y = "Density (log scale)", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "growth_df_main_var_diff_year_log.png", path = graph_dir)

```

**Growth distributions for periods starting in 2014**

* Compare six periods starting in 2014, from 2014–15 through 2014–20
* As in the annual growth density plots, use observations with nonzero growth and an absolute value below 3.5
* Output two figures, with density on a linear and a logarithmic vertical scale

Use the same scales and display ranges as in the annual growth figures.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

growth_long_plot <- sample_growth_tb |>  
  filter(str_sub(year, 6, 7) == "14",
         abs(growth) < 3.5, growth != 0) |> 
ggplot() + 
  geom_density(aes(growth, color = year)) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(
    option = "C",
    labels = year_labels
  ) 

growth_long_plot + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1.0, 1.0)) + 
  labs(
      x = "Growth Rate",
      y = "Density (normal scale)", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "long_term_growth_df_main_var.png", path = graph_dir)
growth_long_plot + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2.0,2.0), ylim = c(10^{-3.0}, 10^{1.5})) + 
  labs(
      x = "Growth Rate",
      y = "Density (log scale)", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "long_term_growth_df_main_var_log.png", path = graph_dir)

```

## 2 Mean Excess Function

Plot mean excess functions separately for annual growth rates and growth rates over periods starting in 2014.
Use data satisfying the common income and age conditions, without applying the zero-growth and absolute-value restrictions used only for the density plots.

Sort `growth` in descending order, $g_{(1)}\geq\cdots\geq g_{(n)}$, and calculate the following expression.

$$\widehat m_j=\frac{1}{j-1}\sum_{i=1}^{j-1}g_{(i)}-g_{(j)}, \qquad j\geq2.$$

Plot the growth threshold on the horizontal axis and `m_excess` on the vertical axis, using colors to distinguish periods.
Display horizontal ranges of 0.1–3 for annual growth and 0.1–4 for growth over periods starting in 2014, with a vertical range of 0–1 in both figures.
Include growth rates outside the displayed range in the calculations.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

mean_excess_plot_f <- \(x){
  x |>
    arrange(desc(growth)) |> 
    group_by(year) |> 
    mutate(m_excess = lag(cummean(growth)) - growth) |> 
  ggplot(aes(growth, m_excess, color = year)) +
    geom_scattermore(pointsize = 1.2) + 
    scale_color_viridis_d(
      option = "C",
      labels = year_labels
    ) 
}

sample_growth_tb |> 
  filter(year %in% c("g_20_19", "g_19_18", "g_18_17", "g_17_16", "g_16_15", "g_15_14")) |>  
  mean_excess_plot_f() + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1, 3.0), ylim = c(0, 1.0)) + 
  labs(
      x = "Threshold u",
      y = "Mean Excess", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "mean_excess_main_var_diff_year.png", path = graph_dir)

sample_growth_tb |>  
  filter(str_sub(year, 6, 7) == "14") |> 
  mean_excess_plot_f() + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1, 4.0), ylim = c(0, 1.0)) + 
  labs(
      x = "Threshold u",
      y = "Mean Excess", 
      color = "Year",
  ) 
ggsave(filename = "mean_excess_main_var_long_growth.png", path = graph_dir)

```
